A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same work. Text and rendered-page comparisons cover the main paper, figures, tables, equations, Appendices A–H, and checklist without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original LLM probing, residual-embedding validation, and neural encoding analyses of the existing Podcast ECoG dataset in Sections 3–5 and Appendices B–E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the reasoning benchmark results in Table 3 and neural encoding analyses in Figures 3–8.

M1.justification: Layer probing, ridge-based residual construction in Algorithm 1, and the neural encoding pipeline are identical. No algorithm, model component, objective, or inference procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same BLiMP and COMPS tasks, 5-hop ProntoQA, WinoGrande, expanded podcast transcripts, and Podcast ECoG data. Task requirements and participant coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: The same raw hidden-state/full-embedding comparisons, bag-of-words controls, and Qwen model comparisons remain in their corresponding experiments. No comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Section 2 retains the same model configurations, 50-token context, four-fold residual regression, five-fold encoding evaluation, neural preprocessing, and word-rate controls. Appendix A's task filtering is also unchanged.

E4.justification: Residual orthogonality and feature-specificity tests, cross-model and cross-benchmark checks, and electrode overlap, lateralization, and regional analyses are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices B–E.

E5.justification: Bootstrap resampling, the 500-shuffle procedure, Fisher transformation, Bonferroni responsiveness criterion, Welch tests, and FDR reporting are identical. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting changes appear.

E6.justification: Reported findings, Tables 1–4, and result figures are unchanged. For example, both report saturation layers 6, 20, and 30 for Qwen2.5-14B and its average reasoning accuracy of 0.770 in Table 3.

T1.justification: The saturation-layer definition, ridge objectives, word-rate variance partitioning, and approximate orthogonality derivation in Section 4.1 are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same claims about reasoning-specific neural prediction, delayed reasoning responses, recruitment beyond classical language areas, and shallow-feature dominance in full embeddings.

C2.justification: The interpretations in Section 6, lateralization qualifications in Appendix E.2, and limitations in Appendix F are identical, including restricted ECoG coverage and uncertainty about representations beyond the reasoning saturation layer.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, hardware, memory requirements, and runtimes remain unchanged, including Appendix G. The code link and dataset/model access information in Appendix H also retain the same targets.

R1.justification: The same 43 cited works and their in-text roles are retained. References [15] and [16] receive publication-record updates, including a revised title for [15]; these and the other metadata edits do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: Edits are confined to the arXiv version/date stamp and bibliographic wording and metadata, including titles, venues, years, page ranges, and a DOI/URL. Scientific prose and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded reference entries reflow the bibliography across pages 11–13: reference [15] moves to page 12, and [29]–[30] move to page 13. All figures, tables, and main-text and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 provides fuller bibliographic records, including conference publication details for [15]–[16] and a DOI/URL for [9], improving source identification and traceability. This is a limited documentation improvement; the scientific methods, evidence, claims, and limitations remain unchanged.
